findings.title: Recovery code consumption/removal only works for local credentials; codes in user storage are never invalidated
findings.body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now returns the user-storage (federated) credential first. The code that follows still assumes a local credential.

- When `allCodesUsed()` is true, it calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. That only touches the local DB, so the federated credential is never removed. The id of a model built via `createFromValues` may also be null or meaningless.
- When validation succeeds through the user storage, `isValid` short-circuits in the storage provider. The local provider's code-consumption logic never runs, and nothing tells the storage that the code was used.

The result is that a recovery code kept in user storage can be reused indefinitely. The login bean keeps asking for the same code number, and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES regeneration path never triggers.

The SPI needs an explicit way to consume or remove codes in user storage, or the authenticator must handle federated credentials separately.

findings.title: getCredentials NPE when user is not in the in-memory map
findings.body:
`getMyUser(user)` can return null; other methods such as `isConfiguredFor` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` guard against this. The new `getCredentials` dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` without a null check.

Any credential listing for a user unknown to the map throws a NullPointerException. That includes the account console, the admin REST API, and `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`.

findings.title: getCredentials now exposes OTP credentials too, changing existing OTP test behaviour
findings.body:
`getCredentials` now also returns the stored OTP `CredentialModel`, which carries a newly generated id. Previously the federated OTP was represented only by the dummy `createUserStorageCredentialRepresentation`. This changes what the account REST endpoint returns for the existing OTP tests, including the credential id used for deletion in `testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin`.

The raw OTP secret is also exposed as the credential value. These side effects on existing OTP behaviour are untested and unrelated to the recovery-codes change.

findings.title: Test does not verify recovery code consumption or reuse rejection
findings.body:
`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` performs only one login with code 0. A second login is the scenario where a federated recovery code should be consumed. The test never checks that a used code is rejected afterwards or that the next code number is requested.

The test provider's `isValid` also never removes used codes. The consumption bug for user-storage codes is therefore neither caught nor documented.
